issues.t: Battery capacity loss on 24 kWh packs
issues.sym: Range shrinks over the years and capacity bars on the dash gauge disappear, faster in hot climates.
issues.why: The battery has no liquid cooling, so heat and frequent fast charging age the cells faster than in liquid-cooled EVs. Early cars drew many complaints about lost capacity.
issues.next: Check the capacity bars and get a battery health report before buying. Limit fast charging in hot weather, park in shade, and ask a dealer whether any capacity warranty remains.

issues.t: Faster than expected loss on 30 kWh packs
issues.sym: Capacity bars drop earlier than expected for the car's age and mileage, and range falls with them.
issues.why: Some 30 kWh packs lost capacity quickly, and some cars also misreported battery health. Nissan released a software update and replaced packs that fell below the capacity warranty threshold.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer for a battery report and the software update, and check whether the car is still within the battery capacity warranty.

issues.t: On-board charger failure - car will not charge
issues.sym: The car stops charging on Level 1 or Level 2, charging faults appear, or the car shows it is plugged in but the battery level never rises.
issues.why: The on-board charger that converts household power for the battery can fail. A weak 12V battery or a station problem can look similar, so they need to be ruled out first.
issues.next: Try a different charger and test the 12V battery first. If it still will not charge, have the on-board charger diagnosed.

issues.t: Weak 12V battery causes no-start and false warnings
issues.sym: The car will not go into Ready, many warning lights come on at once, or brake, ABS or driver-assist messages appear and then clear.
issues.why: The small 12V battery powers the computers that start the car and run the brakes. When it gets weak it can trigger a pile of unrelated fault messages.
issues.next: Test and replace the 12V battery before chasing other faults. If brake warnings stay on after that, get the brakes checked before driving.

issues.t: Passenger occupant sensor failure
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, or the passenger airbag off light behaves oddly.
issues.why: The sensor in the passenger seat that detects a rider can fail, which can turn off the passenger airbag. Repairs often mean replacing seat parts.
issues.next: Have the airbag system scanned soon. Until it is fixed, avoid seating a passenger in front.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may turn off with an adult seated (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light stays on with an adult in the front seat.
issues.why: The occupant sensing system could misread an adult as a child or an empty seat and switch the passenger airbag off. Nissan issued several recalls for sensor and software fixes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the occupant sensor tested. Keep the front seat empty if the light is on with an adult seated.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator may not deploy right (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign. The problem shows up only in a crash.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the passenger front airbag inflator could keep it from deploying properly. Nissan recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the inflator replaced promptly.

issues.t: Passenger airbag connector can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on.
issues.why: The wiring connector for the passenger airbag could disconnect, so the airbag might not deploy. Nissan recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the connector inspected.

issues.t: Brake assist can weaken in extreme cold (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light, a hard pedal that needs much more effort, or weaker braking on very cold days.
issues.why: A relay in the electric brake booster could freeze in extreme cold and reduce power assist. Nissan recalled these cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If braking feels weak or a brake warning stays on, do not drive until it is checked.

issues.t: Inverter can fail and shut the car down (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights come on and the car loses drive power while moving.
issues.why: A circuit board in the inverter that runs the motor could fail on a small group of 2014 cars. Nissan recalled them to replace the inverter.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the car loses power, get off the road safely and have it towed in.

issues.t: Front structural part may be missing welds (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom while driving. The problem would show up only in a crash.
issues.why: A front body structure part on some 2014 cars may have been missing welds, which can reduce crash protection. Nissan recalled them for inspection and repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the inspection done.

issues.t: Slow fast charging on road trips (rapidgate)
issues.sym: The second or third DC fast charge of the day is much slower than the first, and the battery temperature gauge reads high.
issues.why: The battery is still air-cooled. It heats up during highway driving and fast charging, and the car slows charging to protect it.
issues.next: Plan longer stops on trips, charge when the battery is cooler, and use Level 2 charging when you can.

issues.t: Battery can overheat during DC fast charging (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before it happens. A burning smell or smoke during a fast charge is a red flag.
issues.why: On some cars the battery could overheat during Level 3 fast charging, creating a fire risk. Nissan recalled them for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Do not use DC fast chargers until the update is done, and unplug and move away if you smell burning.

issues.t: Car may speed up after leaving cruise control (recall)
issues.sym: After you cancel cruise control and change the drive mode, the car may keep accelerating without you pressing the pedal.
issues.why: A control software error could let the car accelerate unexpectedly in that situation. Nissan recalled these cars to reprogram the control module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the update. Until then, avoid changing drive mode right after cancelling cruise control.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates for no reason
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own with nothing ahead, sometimes at highway speed with ProPILOT on.
issues.why: Owners report false triggers from the forward collision and emergency braking system. No recall covers it, but complaints are well documented.
issues.next: Report each event to a Nissan dealer and NHTSA, ask for camera and radar checks and software updates, and keep the windshield and front sensors clean.

issues.t: Rear camera image goes blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen is black, flickers, shows a distorted picture, or disappears while in reverse.
issues.why: Display settings could hide the image on early cars, software could drop it on 2020 cars, and a camera harness can get damaged on cars through 2022. Nissan issued several recalls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and back up carefully using mirrors until it is fixed.

issues.t: Rear window glass may not stay secured (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or movement of the rear window glass.
issues.why: The rear glass on some 2020 cars may not have been bonded properly and could come loose. Nissan recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the glass inspected.

issues.t: Right-side brake tube can corrode and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, a brake warning light, or brake fluid under the car.
issues.why: A brake line on the right side can corrode and leak fluid, which lowers braking power. Nissan recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the pedal feels soft or you see fluid, do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Battery module can short out - fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Smoke or a burning smell from under the car is an emergency.
issues.why: Internal damage in the high-voltage battery on a small number of new cars could cause a short circuit and fire. Nissan told owners to park outside and not charge until repaired.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. If affected, park outside away from buildings and do not charge until the dealer fixes it.

issues.t: Rear seat belt locking may release early (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat installed with the rear seat belt does not stay tight.
issues.why: The rear outer seat belt retractors can switch out of locking mode too early, so a child seat may not stay secured. Nissan recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Until repaired, install child seats with the LATCH anchors if possible.
